knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine whether $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$. In the affirmative case, find $x_{1}\cdot x_{2}\cdot x_{3}$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b}=x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}$.
$\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ -4 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the definition of span, $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ exactly when coefficients exist such that

$$
x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{b}.
$$

Equating components gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x_{1}+x_{2}-2x_{3} &= 11 \\ -x_{2}+x_{3} &= -4 \\ 4x_{1}-2x_{3} &= 15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix and use elementary row operations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 1 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 & 15\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{3}\leftarrow R_{3}-\left(2\right)R_{1}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 1 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{3}\leftarrow R_{3}-\left(2\right)R_{2}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 1 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Row $3$ gives $0=1$, a contradiction. No coefficients satisfy every component, so $\mathbf{b}\notin \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine whether $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$. In the affirmative case, find $x_{1}\cdot x_{2}\cdot x_{3}$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b}=x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}$.
$\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ -20 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the definition of span, $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ exactly when coefficients exist such that

$$
x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{b}.
$$

Equating components gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1}-3x_{2} &= -7 \\ 2x_{1}-8x_{2} &= -20 \\ -2x_{2}+x_{3} &= -9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix and use elementary row operations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & -7 \\ 2 & -8 & 0 & -20 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{2}\leftarrow R_{2}-\left(2\right)R_{1}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{3}\leftarrow R_{3}-\left(1\right)R_{2}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Back-substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{3} &= \frac{-3}{1} = -3 \\ x_{2} &= \frac{-6}{-2} = 3 \\ x_{1} &= \frac{-7-\left(-3\right)\left(3\right)}{1} = 2\end{aligned}
$$

All component equations hold. Thus $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ and the coefficients are unique. Finally,

$$
x_{1}\cdot x_{2}\cdot x_{3}=\left(2\right)\cdot \left(3\right)\cdot \left(-3\right)=-18.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine whether $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$. In the affirmative case, find $x_{1}\cdot x_{2}\cdot x_{3}$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b}=x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}$.
$\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ -3 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ -8 \\ 20\end{bmatrix}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the definition of span, $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ exactly when coefficients exist such that

$$
x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{b}.
$$

Equating components gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x_{1}-4x_{2}-2x_{3} &= -7 \\ x_{1}-3x_{2} &= -8 \\ -3x_{1}+8x_{2}+x_{3} &= 20\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix and use elementary row operations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & -2 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 & -8 \\ -3 & 8 & 1 & 20\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{2}\leftarrow R_{2}-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)R_{1}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & -2 & -7 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ -3 & 8 & 1 & 20\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{3}\leftarrow R_{3}-\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)R_{1}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & -2 & -7 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & \frac{19}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{3}\leftarrow R_{3}-\left(-2\right)R_{2}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & -2 & -7 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Row $3$ gives $0=\frac{1}{2}$, a contradiction. No coefficients satisfy every component, so $\mathbf{b}\notin \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2},\mathbf{a}_{3}\}$.
